easy.question: Who spoke to Moses at the start of the text?
easy.explanation: The verse opens 'And the Lord spake unto Moses' — so the LORD is the speaker.

easy.question: To whom did Moses command to give God's message according to the verse?
easy.explanation: The verse says 'Command the children of Israel, and say unto them' — the order is directed to the children of Israel.

easy.question: Which land is referred to in the verse?
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly names 'the land of Canaan' — this is the land in view.

medium.question: When, according to the verse, will they receive the land?
answers: when they enter the land of Canaan
after a whole generation has passed
medium.explanation: The verse says 'When ye come into the land of Canaan' — the land is given upon their entering it.

medium.question: In the phrase 'for an inheritance' (verse 2), what does 'inheritance' mean in this context?
answers: a description of a high place
a portion of land given as a hereditary possession
medium.explanation: 'Inheritance' here means a hereditary portion of land — an allotted possession for the people.

medium.question: Who are the recipients intended to receive 'the land' according to the verse?
medium.explanation: The address is to 'the children of Israel' — they are the ones who will receive the land.

challenge.question: What does the phrase 'When ye come into the land' imply about Israel's situation at the time of speaking?
answers: that they are still on the way or just about to enter the land
that they have already lived in the land a long time
that the land is becoming uninhabited territory
challenge.explanation: The future/conditional wording 'When ye come' suggests they are about to enter and are not yet settled there.

challenge.question: Who received the direct command from the LORD according to the verse?
challenge.explanation: The verse begins 'And the Lord spake unto Moses' — the LORD spoke directly to Moses to relay the command.

challenge.question: How does the verse present the status of ownership of the land of Canaan?
answers: as temporary land with no rights attached
as land to be immediately taken without arrangement
as land to be given as an inheritance — allotted as a possession
challenge.explanation: The phrase 'shall fall unto you for an inheritance' indicates the land is to be allotted to them as a possession or inheritance.

answers: as temporary land with no rights attached
as land to be immediately taken without arrangement
as land to be given as an inheritance — allotted as a possession
questions.explanation: The phrase 'shall fall unto you for an inheritance' indicates the land is to be allotted to them as a possession or inheritance.

easy.question: What does verse 3 say about the southern border?
answers: that the border will be 'your south quarter' from the wilderness of Zin by the coast of Edom
laws of labor for the tribe of Judah
a description of a military march through the wilderness
easy.explanation: The verse sets the starting point of the southern border — 'your south quarter shall be from the wilderness of Zin by the coast of Edom.'

easy.question: Which sea is meant by the phrase 'the salt sea' in verse 3?
answers: the Dead Sea (the salty sea in the east)
easy.explanation: The text uses 'the salt sea' to refer to the Dead Sea — the salty inland sea in the east.

easy.question: Do the verses indicate that the border passes through Azmon (עַצְמֹנָה)?
answers: No, it is not mentioned at all
the verses refer to a body part, not a place
Yes — the verse says 'and pass on to Azmon'
easy.explanation: Verse 4 explicitly says 'and pass on to Azmon,' so Azmon is a named point along the border.

medium.question: Where does the border continue after 'your south quarter... from the coast of the salt sea eastward' according to the verses?
answers: upward — by the ascent of Akrabbim continuing to Kadeshbarnea
medium.explanation: The verses describe the border continuing from the south through the ascent of Akrabbim up to Kadeshbarnea and beyond.

medium.question: What does the word 'quarter' mean in the phrase 'your south quarter'?
answers: an edge/side of the region (a border)
medium.explanation: Here 'quarter' denotes a side or edge of the region — the southern boundary area.

medium.question: Which place is mentioned immediately after 'Kadeshbarnea' in verse 4?
medium.explanation: Verse 4 continues 'and shall go on to Hazaraddar' — Hazaraddar appears right after Kadeshbarnea.

challenge.question: Which direction does the phrase 'from the coast of the salt sea eastward' indicate in the border description?
challenge.explanation: 'Eastward' indicates movement toward the east — from the salt sea toward the east.

challenge.question: Which modern wadi is commonly identified with the 'river of Egypt' mentioned in verse 5?
challenge.explanation: Tradition and geographic identification often link the 'river of Egypt' with Wadi el-Arish on the Egypt–Canaan border.

challenge.question: Which phrase in the verse suggests the border rises from the south (or moves upward from the Negev)?
answers: 'from the coast of the salt sea eastward'
'from the south to the ascent of Akrabbim'
'from Azmon to the river of Egypt'
challenge.explanation: The phrase 'from the south to the ascent of Akrabbim' indicates movement upward from the southern starting point.

questions.question: Which direction does the phrase 'from the coast of the salt sea eastward' indicate in the border description?
questions.explanation: 'Eastward' indicates movement toward the east — from the salt sea toward the east.

questions.question: Which modern wadi is commonly identified with the 'river of Egypt' mentioned in verse 5?
questions.explanation: Tradition and geographic identification often link the 'river of Egypt' with Wadi el-Arish on the Egypt–Canaan border.

answers: 'from the coast of the salt sea eastward'

paragraphs.title: The sea and the northern border

easy.question: What is stated in verse 6 as the western border of the land?
easy.explanation: Verse 6 declares that the Great Sea will be the border — this is the border mentioned there.

easy.question: What kind of border is repeated in verse 6?
easy.explanation: The verse speaks of a 'sea border' — the sea is used as the territorial boundary.

easy.question: Which place is mentioned in verse 7 as the northern endpoint of the border?
easy.explanation: Verse 7 names 'Mount Hor' as the point marking the end of the northern border.

medium.question: What does the word 'border' mean in the context 'north border'?
answers: a boundary or dividing line between territories
medium.explanation: Here 'border' refers to a territorial limit — the dividing line of the land.

medium.question: According to verse 7, what is the extent of the north border?
answers: from the Great Sea to the Jordan
from the Great Sea to the Dead Sea
from the Great Sea to Mount Hor
medium.explanation: The verse states the north border runs 'from the Great Sea' to 'Mount Hor' — that is its extent.

medium.question: In which verse is 'Mount Hor' named as the northern point?
medium.explanation: 'Mount Hor' appears in verse 7 as the northern endpoint, not in verse 6.

challenge.question: By common biblical-geographic understanding, which sea is likely the 'Great Sea' mentioned in these verses?
challenge.explanation: In biblical geography the 'Great Sea' usually refers to the Mediterranean Sea — the great sea to the west.

challenge.question: Why does the verse repeat the word 'border' several times in verse 6?
answers: to indicate there are many internal borders
to emphasize that the sea is the western boundary of the land
to say the border will change each generation
challenge.explanation: The repetition underscores that the Great Sea is the clear western boundary of the land.

challenge.question: What is a reasonable explanation for the doubled name 'Mount Hor' in verse 7?
answers: it is the name of a city on a mountain
it is a proper place-name — 'Mount Hor' (a formal name)
challenge.explanation: The doubled form functions as a proper name (Mount Hor) rather than indicating multiple distinct mountains.

questions.question: By common biblical-geographic understanding, which sea is likely the 'Great Sea' mentioned in these verses?
questions.explanation: In biblical geography the 'Great Sea' usually refers to the Mediterranean Sea — the great sea to the west.

answers: to indicate there are many internal borders
to emphasize that the sea is the western boundary of the land
to say the border will change each generation
questions.explanation: The repetition underscores that the Great Sea is the clear western boundary of the land.

questions.question: What is a reasonable explanation for the doubled name 'Mount Hor' in verse 7?
answers: it is the name of a city on a mountain
it is a proper place-name — 'Mount Hor' (a formal name)
questions.explanation: The doubled form functions as a proper name (Mount Hor) rather than indicating multiple distinct mountains.

easy.question: According to verse 9, which point is set as 'your north border'?
easy.explanation: Verse 9 states 'and the border shall go on to Ziphron... this shall be your north border' — Ziphron is named as the north point.

easy.question: What does verse 12 say about the outlets of the Jordan?
answers: that they flow to the Mediterranean
that they are the Dead Sea
that they drain into the Sea of Galilee
easy.explanation: Verse 12 says 'and the goings out of it shall be at the salt sea' — the Dead Sea is the outlet referenced.

easy.question: Which lake is mentioned in verse 11 in connection with the border descending?
easy.explanation: Verse 11 refers to 'the sea of Chinnereth' — that is the Sea of Galilee.

medium.question: In the phrase 'your east border' (verse 10), which compass direction does 'east' refer to?
medium.explanation: 'East' (or 'eastward') here denotes movement or orientation toward the sunrise — toward the east.

medium.question: What does the word 'border' mean in the context 'the goings out of the border shall be to Zedad'?
medium.explanation: Here 'border' means a territorial boundary; the phrase lists boundary points and directions.

medium.question: What is the general movement of the border as described in verses 8–12?
answers: the description begins in the east and goes north
the description circles the land with no order
it starts in the north and goes down to the south as far as the Dead Sea
medium.explanation: The verses list northern points then describe the border descending southward to the Jordan and the Dead Sea.

challenge.question: The ancient city Ziphron (Ziphron/Ziphronah) mentioned in these verses corresponds today to which modern country?
challenge.explanation: Ziphron (near Sidon) is an ancient coastal city located in modern Lebanon.

challenge.question: What does the phrase 'the coast shall go down from Shepham to Riblah' suggest the verb 'go down' means here?
challenge.explanation: In this geographic context 'go down' means to descend or move southward along the border.

challenge.question: How should 'the goings out of it' be understood in verse 12: 'and the goings out of it shall be at the salt sea'?
answers: the places to which the river drains / flows out
challenge.explanation: 'The goings out of it' refers to where the river drains — the places to which it empties; here the Dead Sea.

questions.question: The ancient city Ziphron (Ziphron/Ziphronah) mentioned in these verses corresponds today to which modern country?
questions.explanation: Ziphron (near Sidon) is an ancient coastal city located in modern Lebanon.

answers: the places to which the river drains / flows out

easy.question: Who commanded the children of Israel at the opening of this section?
easy.explanation: Verse 13 begins 'And Moses commanded the children of Israel' — Moses is the one giving the command.

easy.question: What does verse 13 'This is the land which ye shall inherit' describe?
answers: the land to be given over to the Canaanites
the land to be apportioned to the Israelite settlement — an inheritance
easy.explanation: The verse describes the land that will be apportioned to Israel as an inheritance.

easy.question: According to verses 14–15, who have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan?
answers: the children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh
easy.explanation: The verses name Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh as those who received their inheritance beyond the Jordan.

medium.question: What does the phrase 'inherit by lot' mean in this context (verse 13)?
answers: allocated by lot / apportioned as the LORD commanded
medium.explanation: 'Inherit by lot' means the land is apportioned by drawing lots, as directed by the LORD.

medium.question: What does 'half the tribe' mean in verse 14 'and half the tribe of Manasseh'?
answers: half of Manasseh — part of the tribe received a separate portion
half of each other tribe's land
medium.explanation: It indicates the tribe of Manasseh was divided — part of the tribe received land on that side of the Jordan.

medium.question: What does the phrase 'on this side Jordan near Jericho eastward, toward the sunrising' describe (verse 15)?
answers: the side of the Jordan eastward, beyond the river
east of the Jordan toward the sea
medium.explanation: The phrase specifies the inheritances were on the eastern side of the Jordan, near Jericho, toward the sunrise (east).

challenge.question: What can be inferred from 'half the tribe of Manasseh' about the settlement pattern of Manasseh?
answers: that Manasseh was destroyed and reduced to half a tribe
that Manasseh was divided into two groups — part settled east of the Jordan and part elsewhere
that only half of Manasseh had land rights
challenge.explanation: The wording implies the tribe was split, with part of Manasseh settling on one side of the Jordan and the rest elsewhere.

challenge.question: According to the verses, how many tribal units received their inheritance beyond the Jordan?
answers: two full tribes and a half unit (2.5) — two tribes and a half tribe
challenge.explanation: The text mentions 'two tribes and a half tribe' — i.e., two full tribes plus half of a tribe.

challenge.question: In modern geography, where were most of the inheritances described as 'beyond Jordan' located?
answers: on the eastern side of the Jordan River — in territory of modern Jordan
challenge.explanation: 'Beyond Jordan' refers to the east side of the Jordan River, generally corresponding to parts of modern Jordan.

questions.question: What can be inferred from 'half the tribe of Manasseh' about the settlement pattern of Manasseh?
answers: that Manasseh was destroyed and reduced to half a tribe
that Manasseh was divided into two groups — part settled east of the Jordan and part elsewhere
that only half of Manasseh had land rights
questions.explanation: The wording implies the tribe was split, with part of Manasseh settling on one side of the Jordan and the rest elsewhere.

answers: two full tribes and a half unit (2.5) — two tribes and a half tribe
questions.explanation: The text mentions 'two tribes and a half tribe' — i.e., two full tribes plus half of a tribe.

answers: on the eastern side of the Jordan River — in territory of modern Jordan
questions.explanation: 'Beyond Jordan' refers to the east side of the Jordan River, generally corresponding to parts of modern Jordan.

easy.explanation: The passage opens 'And the Lord spake unto Moses' — the LORD is the speaker.

easy.question: Which two persons are named in verse 17?
answers: Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun
easy.explanation: Verse 17 names Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun as the men who shall divide the land.

easy.question: How many princes are to be taken from each tribe to divide the land according to verse 18?
easy.explanation: Verse 18 commands that one prince of every tribe be taken to divide the land.

medium.question: How was it determined who would handle the allotment of the land for each tribe?
answers: by the selection of all the people together
one prince from each tribe was taken to handle the division
medium.explanation: The verse specifies that one prince from each tribe is to be chosen to handle the allotment.

medium.question: What does the word 'prince' mean in the phrase 'one prince of every tribe'?
answers: a head or representative of the tribe
medium.explanation: 'Prince' here denotes a tribal leader or representative — the head of the tribe chosen for the task.

medium.question: What is the significance of naming Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun in verse 17?
answers: that they are two new tribes
that they are responsible for matters of allotment and distribution of the land
that they were sent to build the tabernacle
medium.explanation: They are named as the officials charged with overseeing the division and allotment of the land.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the repetition 'one prince' in the verse about how the land distribution was organized?
answers: only one tribe will get an inheritance
a single representative from each tribe is chosen to ensure equal representation
every individual will receive land personally without representatives
challenge.explanation: Emphasizing 'one prince of every tribe' indicates a system of equal tribal representation for the division.

challenge.question: In the verse 'These are the names of the men which shall divide the land unto you' — who performs the action 'shall divide' according to the syntax?
challenge.explanation: The syntax shows the men listed (Eleazar and Joshua) are the ones who will divide the land.

challenge.question: Why might Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun have been chosen to oversee the allotments historically/culturally?
answers: because they combined religious and civic/military authority — priestly and civil leadership
because they were the first judges of Israel
because they were foreigners living in the land
challenge.explanation: Eleazar was the leading priest and Joshua the national leader; together they provided religious and administrative authority for the allotment.

answers: only one tribe will get an inheritance
a single representative from each tribe is chosen to ensure equal representation
every individual will receive land personally without representatives
questions.explanation: Emphasizing 'one prince of every tribe' indicates a system of equal tribal representation for the division.

easy.question: Who is named as the leader of the tribe of Judah in verse 19?
easy.explanation: Verse 19 explicitly names Caleb son of Jephunneh as the leader for Judah.

easy.question: Hanniel son of Ephod is prince of which tribe?
easy.explanation: Verse 23 identifies Hanniel son of Ephod as the prince for the tribe of Manasseh.

easy.question: What general command appears in verse 29 regarding the land of Canaan?
answers: to give the land of Canaan as an inheritance to the children of Israel
easy.explanation: Verse 29 states that these are the ones the LORD commanded to divide the inheritance to the children of Israel in the land of Canaan.

medium.question: What does 'prince' mean in the context 'and unto the tribe of Zebulun a prince Elizaphan'?
medium.explanation: 'Prince' indicates the tribal leader or representative appointed for that tribe.

medium.question: Which tribes in this list are explicitly descendants of Joseph?
medium.explanation: The passages name both Manasseh and Ephraim, who are the two tribes descended from Joseph.

medium.question: Why is the tribe of Levi not included in this list of allotting leaders?
answers: because they were expelled from Canaan
because the Levites did not receive a territorial inheritance like the other tribes
because they are listed elsewhere here
medium.explanation: The Levites did not receive a normal tribal territory; they had cities and religious duties instead, so they are not included among land allotters.

challenge.question: How many princes/leaders are listed in verses 19–28?
challenge.explanation: Verses 19–28 list ten tribal leaders (one for each land-receiving tribe), so the total is 10.

challenge.question: What pattern is visible in the order of tribes listed (verses 19–28)?
challenge.explanation: The list begins with Judah (southern) and ends with Naphtali (northern), indicating a south-to-north order.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from this list of names about their role?
answers: that they were military commanders for the invasion of Canaan
that they were representatives who would receive and represent the inheritance for their tribe
that they were prominent commercial figures
challenge.explanation: The context says these are the men whom the LORD commanded to divide the inheritance — they are tribal representatives for allotment.
